explain: A rule: a selector (which elements), then { } with declarations. A declaration is property: value; All of CSS is rules.
example: po.wor: css/style.css is a list of rules.
remember: WHO { WHAT: HOW; }: selector, property, value.

explain: Selectors: a tag name, a .class, an #id, or a combination (nav a = an a inside a nav).
example: po.wor: .bubble, header, nav a.
remember: . = class (many), # = id (one). A space = "inside".

syntax:
p { color: red; }
p { color: blue; }  /* wins */
explain: The cascade: when two rules set the same property, the more specific selector wins (#id > .class > tag); if equal, the later one wins.
example: Why a style "doesn't work": another rule beats it.
remember: Specific beats general; later beats earlier.

explain: The box model: every element is a box. Content, then padding (inside), border, then margin (outside).
example: po.wor: the cards and bubbles.
remember: Inside out: content, padding, border, margin (like a framed picture on a wall).

explain: A custom property (--name) stores a value; var(--name) reads it. Change it in one place, it changes everywhere.
example: po.wor: theme colours (light and dark).
remember: -- makes it, var() uses it.

explain: A pseudo-class is a selector with :state added. The rule shape stays the same.
example: po.wor: links underline on hover.
remember: : = "when it is…" (hovered, focused, first).

explain: An at-rule wraps normal rules. @media means "only use these rules when the screen matches".
example: po.wor: the phone layout.
remember: @media = an if around rules.

explain: @keyframes is a rule wrapping mini-rules (the selectors are times). The animation property then uses it by name.
example: po.wor: the bouncing logo.
remember: Name the moves in @keyframes, play them with animation.
builtFrom: at-rule + declarations + a value that names it

explain: Size, space inside (padding), a line around (border), space outside (margin).
example: Spacing out cards so they do not touch.
remember: Box model, inside out: content → padding → border → margin.

explain: Puts the children in a row with gaps between them, centered top to bottom.
example: A navigation bar with a logo and links.

explain: A grid of 3 equal columns. 1fr means one share of the free space.
example: A photo gallery.
remember: fr = a fraction (share) of the free space.

explain: The font, its size, and the space between lines.
example: Making a long article easy to read.

explain: Text and background colors, and a different color while the mouse is over it.
example: Buttons that react when you point at them.

syntax:
.parent { position: relative; }
.badge  { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; }
explain: absolute places an element by its nearest parent that has position: relative.
example: A red notification count on the corner of an icon.
remember: absolute moves to the nearest relative parent. Relative = the anchor, absolute = the boat.

explain: Rules inside only apply on screens 600px wide or less.
example: One column on phones, three columns on laptops.
remember: max-width = "up to this wide" (phones). min-width = "at least this wide" (big screens).

explain: Picks links inside .nav, but only while the mouse is over them.
example: Menu links that underline when you point at them.

explain: Select by tag name, by .class, or by #id.
example: Styling all paragraphs, some boxes, one heading.

syntax:
nav a { color: white; }
ul > li { list-style: none; }
explain: A space means "anywhere inside". > means "direct child only".
example: Links only inside the menu.
remember: space = any child or grandchild. > = direct child only.

explain: A comma gives several selectors the same style.
example: All headings at once.

syntax:
input[type="email"] { border-color: blue; }
a[href^="https"] { color: green; }
explain: [attr="value"] selects by attribute. ^= means "starts with".
example: Styling only email inputs.
remember: ^= starts with, $= ends with, *= contains.

explain: Pick elements by their position. even/odd or 2n+1 also work.
example: Striped table rows.

explain: ::before and ::after add content before or after an element using CSS.
example: Icons and arrows without extra HTML.
remember: ::before = first thing inside, ::after = last thing inside. They need content to show.

explain: :focus is the box you're typing in, :disabled is a turned-off button, :not() excludes something.
example: Showing which field is active.

explain: * selects every element.
example: A reset at the top of a stylesheet.
remember: border-box: the width you set includes padding and border. Sizes stop surprising you.

explain: Shorthand: two values = top/bottom then left/right; four = top, right, bottom, left (clockwise).
example: Spacing around and inside boxes.
remember: Padding is inside the border (cushion), margin is outside (personal space).

explain: margin: 0 auto centers a block that has a width. max-width stops it overflowing on phones.
example: A centered page column.

explain: border is width, style and color. border-radius rounds the corners.
example: Cards and buttons.

explain: min-height sets the smallest height. overflow: auto adds a scrollbar when content is too big.
example: A full-screen section, a scrolling list.

explain: block takes a full line, inline flows with text, inline-block flows but can have a width. none hides it.
example: Hiding a menu, sizing badges.

explain: justify-content spaces items along the row, align-items lines them up across it.
example: A header with logo left and menu right.
remember: justify = along the row (main way), align = across it.

explain: flex-direction: column stacks items top to bottom. gap adds space between them.
example: A form with fields under each other.

explain: flex: 1 makes an item take the leftover space. flex-wrap lets items go to the next line.
example: A search box that fills the bar; tags that wrap.

explain: Makes as many 200px+ columns as fit. It changes by itself with the screen size.
example: A photo gallery that works on any screen.
remember: auto-fill + minmax = "as many columns as fit, each at least this wide".

explain: span 2 takes two columns. 1 / -1 goes from the first to the last column.
example: A big featured card in a grid.

explain: place-items: center puts the content in the exact middle.
example: Centering a login box on the screen.

syntax:
.top-bar { position: sticky; top: 0; }
.chat { position: fixed; bottom: 20px; right: 20px; }
explain: sticky stays on screen once you scroll to it. fixed always stays in the same spot on the screen.
example: Sticky headers, a chat button.

explain: z-index decides what is on top. Bigger numbers go in front.
example: Menus that cover the page.

explain: rem is relative to the html font size. line-height is the space between lines.
example: Easy-to-read text.

explain: Boldness, alignment, capital letters, and space between letters.
example: Small labels like "NEW".

explain: Load a font from Google Fonts, then use it. The second name is a backup.
example: Using a custom font.

explain: Keeps text on one line and adds "..." when it doesn't fit.
example: Long file names in a list.

explain: Four ways to write a color. The last number in rgba is see-through-ness (0 to 1).
example: Matching brand colors.

explain: A gradient fades from one color to another.
example: Colorful banners.

explain: box-shadow: x, y, blur, color. It makes the box look lifted.
example: Cards that float above the page.

explain: --name stores a value. var(--name) uses it. Change it once, it changes everywhere.
example: Theme colors.

explain: transition makes changes smooth instead of instant.
example: Buttons that fade when you hover.
remember: Put transition on the normal state, not the :hover one, so it animates both ways.

explain: transform moves, grows, or turns an element without moving others.
example: A playful hover effect.
remember: transform moves the drawing, not the layout: nothing around it shifts.

explain: @keyframes describes an animation; animation plays it.
example: A loading spinner.
remember: Write the keyframes once (the dance), play it with animation (press play).

explain: cursor changes the mouse pointer. opacity makes an element see-through.
example: Showing something is clickable or disabled.

explain: min-width rules apply on screens this wide or wider. Start with phones, add for big screens.
example: Mobile-first layouts.

explain: Images shrink to fit their box and keep their shape.
example: Photos that never overflow on phones.

explain: clamp(min, preferred, max). vw is 1% of the screen width.
example: Headings that grow with the screen.

explain: Applies when the computer is in dark mode.
example: Dark mode.

explain: calc() does math with units. aspect-ratio keeps a shape; object-fit: cover fills it without stretching.
example: Video thumbnails.

explain: attr() reads an attribute from the HTML and shows its value as text. A tooltip with no JavaScript.
example: po.wor header: data-tip="Home?" on the logo becomes the message bubble.
remember: attr() = "read this tag's attribute". data-tip in HTML → attr(data-tip) in CSS.

explain: CSS counts for you: counter-reset starts at 0, counter-increment adds 1 on each row, counter() shows the number.
example: po.wor planner: the line numbers on the left, like a code editor.
remember: Like a tally clicker: reset it, click once per row, read it.

explain: Percent steps give an animation many stops, not only from and to. 30% means 30% of the way through the time.
example: po.wor: the logo, the • and the box bounce when you point at them.
remember: 0% = start, 100% = end; the steps in between are stops along the way.

explain: transform-origin is the point it turns around (the hinge). cubic-bezier is a custom speed curve; a number above 1 makes it go past the end and spring back.
example: po.wor header: the box lid swings open on its corner, a little springy.
remember: origin = where the pin goes in. In cubic-bezier, a number over 1 = overshoot (springy).

explain: transition-delay waits before the change starts. Put it on the hover rule and it only waits on the way in.
example: po.wor: the message bubbles appear after a short pause, so they don't flash when the mouse passes by.
remember: delay = wait, then go.

explain: Clicks and hovers go straight through the element to whatever is under it.
example: po.wor: the message bubbles never block a click.
remember: none = a ghost: the mouse passes right through.

explain: top: 100% puts it right under its parent; calc adds a 10px gap. The parent needs position: relative.
example: po.wor: each message bubble sits just under its link.
remember: 100% of the parent's height = just below it.

explain: The first element of its tag type among its siblings.
example: po.wor homepage: no line above the first entry.
remember: first-child = the first kid. first-of-type = the first kid of that kind.

explain: + picks an element that comes right after another one. A gap between boxes, but none above the first.
example: po.wor Japanese page: space between the white panels.
remember: + = "the one right next to it".

explain: Moves the underline a little lower, so it doesn't touch the letters.
example: po.wor homepage: the project links.
remember: offset = how far below the text.

explain: ch is the width of the "0" character, good for numbers and monospace text. em is the element's font size, so it grows with the text.
example: po.wor: planner line numbers are 3ch wide; homepage icons are 1.5em.
remember: ch = characters wide. em = "as big as the font".

explain: min() uses the smaller value. svh is 1% of the screen height on phones when the browser bars are showing.
example: po.wor Japanese page: the writing paper is never wider than the screen or too tall to see.
remember: min() = a ceiling: never bigger than the smallest choice. svh = small viewport height.

explain: cqi is 1% of the container's width, so text grows with the box, not with the whole window.
example: po.wor Japanese page: the letters in the squares grow with the paper.
remember: cqi = container query inline (% of the box). vw = % of the window.

explain: 7 equal columns. minmax(0, 1fr) lets them get narrow even when a word is long.
example: po.wor planner: the week view, Monday to Sunday.
remember: 7 days = repeat(7, …). minmax(0, …) = "you may get tiny".

explain: In a flex row, margin-left: auto takes all the free space on the left, pushing the item to the right.
example: po.wor header: the planner • sits on the right, next to the box.
remember: An auto margin eats all the empty space.

explain: flex: none keeps an item at its own size. min-width: 0 lets a flex item shrink, so long text wraps instead of sticking out.
example: po.wor planner: the line number stays fixed, the text takes the rest.
remember: Flex items won't shrink below their content until you say min-width: 0.

explain: Lines up one item differently from the others in a flex row.
example: po.wor planner: a --- divider sits in the middle of its row.
remember: align-items = for all the kids, align-self = for one kid.

explain: A display rule in CSS beats the hidden attribute, so the element would still show. This rule makes hidden work again.
example: po.wor planner: the phone bullet bar.
remember: CSS display beats HTML hidden. [hidden] { display: none } puts hidden back in charge.

syntax:
.row { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: break-word; }
.sample { white-space: pre-line; }
explain: pre-wrap keeps your spaces and line breaks as typed, and still wraps at the edge. pre-line keeps only the line breaks. break-word breaks a very long word so it fits.
example: po.wor: planner lines keep their spaces; Japanese samples keep their paragraphs.
remember: pre = keep it as typed. wrap = but still wrap at the edge.

explain: Makes a textarea look like plain text: no border, no focus ring, no drag corner. ::placeholder styles the grey hint text.
example: po.wor planner: the line you type on looks the same as the other lines.
remember: resize: none removes the corner handle. ::placeholder is a pseudo-element, like ::before.

explain: Buttons don't take the page's font on their own. inherit makes them use their parent's font and colour.
example: po.wor: the planner buttons look like the rest of the text.
remember: inherit = "use what my parent has".

explain: filter: invert(1) flips every colour: black becomes white. Handy for a black logo on a dark page.
example: po.wor: the logo in dark mode.
remember: invert = turn it inside out (1 = fully, 0 = not at all).

explain: Only when the device can hover (a mouse or trackpad). Phones can't point, so they skip these rules.
example: po.wor: the planner header hides only on a computer.
remember: hover: hover = "has a pointer". Hide hover-only things from phones.

explain: :focus-within matches an element when it, or anything inside it, has keyboard focus. Two selectors with a comma share one rule.
example: po.wor: the hidden planner header comes back when you Tab into it.
remember: focus-within = "focus is somewhere inside me".
